title: South Florida Events This Week: Free and Cheap First
igCaption:
Free first: James Turrell’s “Blue Sea Sky” at Superblue Miami uses complimentary on-site reservations.
Cheap museum stop: Yuko Mohri’s first solo U.S. museum exhibition is at the Bass through May 30, 2027.
Brightline is running late-night trains after over 15 Kaseya Center concerts. What should we cover next?

Sources: Miami New Times, Secret Miami, Eventbrite, Local 10, Wikipedia

#MiamiEvents #SouthFlorida #MiamiGuide #ThingsToDo

scenes.text: Free art, late-night trains, sunflowers, and a centennial festival are on the South Florida calendar this week.
Start free at Superblue Miami. James Turrell’s “Blue Sea Sky” is a room-sized color installation at 1101 NW 23rd St. Access requires a complimentary on-site reservation, first come, first served.
scenes.caption: Start free at Superblue Miami. James Turrell’s “Blue Sea Sky” is a room-sized color installation at 1101 NW 23rd St. Access requires a complimentary on-site reservation, first come, first served.

scenes.text: For a low-cost museum stop, the Bass has Yuko Mohri’s “Unviolated Imperfection.” It is her first solo U.S. museum exhibition, spread across three galleries, with tickets from $8 to $15 through May 30, 2027.
scenes.caption: For a low-cost museum stop, the Bass has Yuko Mohri’s “Unviolated Imperfection.” It is her first solo U.S. museum exhibition, spread across 3 galleries, with tickets from $8 to $15 through May 30, 2027.

scenes.text: Brightline brought back late-night service for Kaseya Center shows through the end of the year. MiamiCentral sits less than a mile from the arena, and riders should book the Concert Connect return trip. If you’re on that Brightline run, check NEAR after the show for familiar faces.

scenes.text: Pepper Ranch has its Sunflower Viewing Event from Friday, October 2, through Sunday, October 11. The daily window runs 9 AM to 2 PM.
scenes.caption: Pepper Ranch has its Sunflower Viewing Event from Friday, Oct. 2, through Sunday, Oct. 11. The daily window runs 9 AM to 2 PM.

scenes.text: North Miami Beach is celebrating 100 years with a centennial festival focused on its diverse communities. The city was originally named Fulford-by-the-Sea in 1926 and renamed North Miami Beach in 1931.

scenes.text: Which one are you doing, and what should we cover next? It’s funny how you can spend a whole night at a South Florida event and still never catch the name of the person standing next to you—that’s the kind of gap NEAR fills.
